correctness.rationale: The proof independently establishes that nonempty out-neighborhood equality exactly defines the cyclic fibers with three variable names. For k>=3, local k-witness formulas recover each clipped fiber cardinality; three-variable closed walks recover quotient length and cyclic order, with local free-variable scopes checked. A permanent k-pebble strategy preserves partial injections fiberwise whenever clipped necklaces agree. At k=2, the universal semiadjacency predicate P(x) detects precisely singleton fibers on a triangle quotient; the four value classes are distinguished by two-variable sentences, and the generic/no-P class has an indefinite two-pebble response for equality, forward arc, reverse arc and nonedge. Width one is trivial. Burnside and weighted orbit enumeration follow by direct rotation fixed-point counts. The two included standard-library programs replayed and agreed on 1403 k-variable pair comparisons, 765 structural graph instances, and exact enumerations. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove infinite claims. A third direct formula-evaluator script checks 90 decorated closed-walk sentences and 308 local fiber-size formulas, including lexical variable shadowing, supplementing the 1403 two-/three-/four-variable pair tests and 78,070 twin checks.

value.rationale: A natural infinite class of directed independent-fiber graph substitutions admits a complete exact classification in every counting-free finite-variable fragment. Four exceptional two-variable theories collapse all longer quotient cycles, whereas three variables recover the entire quotient and arbitrary clipped cyclic fiber profile. The proof gives a nontrivial definability threshold from equality of out-neighborhoods, an indefinite pebble strategy, strictness at every variable width, canonical minimum representatives, and weighted necklace polynomials counting them by order. These constitute structural and enumerative information not merely an arbitrary finite recomputation; they identify the precise logical information loss in a graph substitution widely used in combinatorics. The relation to previously known cyclic leaf substitutions is explicitly distinguished.
